narrative.overview: LightCues is a piece of show hardware: a matte dark panel with legends silkscreened onto it, values in recessed display slots, and keys you press. It sits in a dark venue during the show, so it is calm, legible and deliberate. Nothing moves or glows unless the state changed, and every mark means something. It shares this system with its LiveCues siblings, [VideoCues](https://github.com/GiorgosKoulouris/livecues-videocues) and [Reaper Remote](https://github.com/GiorgosKoulouris/livecues-reaper-remote). VideoCues is the closest, since it is also a Windows desktop app. Hex values stay identical across the three. LightCues adds sections for its own surfaces: the Fallback Panel, Perform, the Scene list and editor, the Preview and Stage Plan, Blackout and Blind. The density is a working rack unit's. It assumes the user knows DMX, and fits a lot on one screen like a console. Perform is the exception: its controls grow to gig size.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only. A light theme stays possible because tokens are named by role.
Flat: depth is tone (Bar, Chassis, Display) plus 1px rules. No shadows, blur or gradients. The only exceptions are a lit LED's 6px halo and inset hard lines.
Square corners everywhere. A key has one chamfered corner, top right, 8px, cut with `clip-path`.
One Signal Orange: the one lit key, keyboard focus, selection and the selected view.
State is always a drawn shape plus a word, never colour alone: disc, ring, triangle, square.
IBM Plex Sans for anything printed on the panel, IBM Plex Mono for values the machine reports.

rules.name: The Lit-Key Rule
rules.body: At most one Signal-filled key per view, and only for the forward action. Every other primary button is a plain key.

rules.name: The LED Rule
rules.body: Green, red and amber only report state, and always appear beside a drawn shape and a word. They never fill a key face or tint a background.

rules.name: The Dark Room Rule
rules.body: Text is Legend or Legend Dim. No new greys, no new hues, no hex outside `tokens.css`. The one exception is Preview and Stage Plan data (see below).

rules.name: The Silkscreen Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels the panel is a legend: small, spaced, upper-case, Legend Dim. Anything the machine reports is in Mono. Words the operator acts on (key labels) are sentence-case Sans.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes or is read as a value is Mono with tabular figures, so it does not shift as it changes.

rules.name: The Flat-Panel Rule
rules.body: No shadows, blur or gradients. The only exceptions are a lit LED's 6px halo and inset hard lines.

rules.name: The Sunk-Is-On Rule
rules.body: A pressed-in look is reserved for state. A key sinks only while something it controls is on.

dos: Do take every colour, size and spacing from the tokens in `src/renderer/src/ui/tokens.css`. Add a token rather than hard-coding a value.
Do pair every state colour with a drawn shape and an upper-case word.
Do put values the machine reports in Mono with tabular figures.
Do print the keyboard key on any control that has one.
Do keep Perform's targets at gig size.
Do keep hex values identical to the sibling apps.
donts: Don't light more than one key per view, or fill a key red or green.
Don't add shadows, blur, gradients, rounded corners or illustrations.
Don't use colour alone to report state.
Don't add a light theme surface or any large bright area.
Don't load fonts, icons or images from the network. Everything ships with the app.
Don't let the Sidebar, top bar or Fallback Panel scroll out of view.
